title: PowerShell Script Block Referencing Scanning Interface Internals
detection_hypothesis: If script scanning is targeted for interference, the logged script block will reference the internal type and field names of the scanning interface.

field_semantics.ScriptBlockText: Decoded PowerShell script block text as executed.

collection_prerequisites: Script block logging is enabled through Group Policy or registry configuration.
PowerShell operational log collection is enabled on the endpoint.
expected_collection_gaps: PowerShell version 2 engines do not emit script block logs.
Very large script blocks are split across multiple events.
normalization_assumptions: ScriptBlockText contains the decoded script text as executed.
ingestion_differences: Multi-part script blocks may need reassembly before matching.
Some pipelines strip newlines from ScriptBlockText.
retention_considerations: Script block logging is moderate to high volume; 90 days is a common target.
expected_volume: Very low; effectively zero outside research hosts.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches are confined to named research or validation hosts and to a small set of authors. Tune on the host name and script path, and treat any match outside those hosts as an incident.
tuning_guidance: Restrict exclusions to the research host names. Do not exclude the interface type names, because they carry the whole signal.
test_strategy: Positive cases pair the interface type names with reflective field modification verbs. Negative cases include the type name alone and the verbs alone.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1685.
